source.citation: Historic American Buildings Survey. John J. Glessner House, 1800 S. Prairie Avenue, Chicago, Cook County, Illinois. HABS IL-1015 (HABS ILL,16-CHIG,17-), measured drawings, sheets 1-6: sheet 1 title sheet with neighborhood plan (1" = 100', buildings from Bromley 1892), sheet 2 first floor plan (3/32" = 1'-0", del. Robert C. Giebner, June 1963), sheet 3 second floor plan (3/32" = 1'-0", del. Giebner), sheet 4 Section A-A (1/4" = 1'-0", del. Janis J. Erins), sheet 5 masonry details (1/4" = 1'-0", del. David T. Van Zanten), sheet 6 front (east) elevation (photogrammetric, photographed April 6, 1965, plotted at the Ohio State University under Perry E. Borchers, drawn by Eric N. DeLony). Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division.
what_it_does_not_supply: a north (18th Street), west (alley) or courtyard elevation: none of the six sheets draws one, so heights on those faces come from sheets 4-5 and the 1888 photograph or are reconstructed
a roof plan: the E-W extent of the pyramid-roofed element in Section A-A, the stable roof and the roofs over the bays are not drawn
anything about 1904 as such: it is a 1963-1965 record
the colour of any material, or door and window hardware beyond what sheets 5-6 draw
lot lines: no sheet draws the property boundary except the thin south boundary wall on sheets 2-3
what_it_supplies: the plan envelope of the house: 161'-3" along E. 18th Street, 74'-0" along Prairie Avenue, the 26'-6" east wing, the 35'-6" by 59'-9" west (stable) wing, the 26'-10" north range and the 47'-2" / 99'-3" courtyard (sheets 2-3 dimension strings)
courtyard-side projections: the round stair tower, the 9'-6" radius hall bow and the dining-room bay (sheet 2)
the east (Prairie Avenue) facade opening by opening, and its heights: 24.30 ft to the second-floor window soffits and 48.62 ft to the top of the north chimney above the door sill (sheet 6)
floor levels, eave and ridge heights and the roof profile of the north range, and the dormers, tower and eave of the east wing's courtyard slope (sheet 4)
the 18th Street entrance arch, the 18th Street carriage doorway, the Prairie Avenue entrance and the granite coursing (sheet 5)
the street-face openings of the north and west walls at first- and second-floor level, as gaps in the plans (sheets 2-3)
